newsitem.title: UK: Canadian Pacific hopes to see Lykes deal by mid-Ju.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific hopes to see Lykes deal by mid-Ju.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd said Monday it will push ahead with its acquisition of US container shipping company Lykes Lines despite failing to gain US government vessel operating subsidies.

UK-based subsidiary of the Canadian group, CP Ships, said the $34 million take-over of Lykes, which has been operating under Chapter XI bankruptcy protection since October 1995, was still "expected to close shortly."
CP Ships president Ray Miles said: "We consider that the transaction still makes sense for us without subsidy." A spokesman added he hopes to see the take-over completed by mid-July.

The US Maritime Administration (Marad) on Friday rejected the transfer of operating subsidies of about $2 million a year for three of the four 2,800 teu Lykes container ships which CP Ships intends to take on long time charter.

Marad rejected the subsidies which are given for maintaining ships under the US flag with US crews ready for military use during times of national emergency on the grounds that Canadian Pacific was unable to satisfy its proof of citizenship requirements.
However, Miles said CP Ships still intended to maintain the US flag requirements and commitment to the military defence programme despite the rejection.
Miles added that a new US company, Lykes Lines Ltd, had already been set up to operate as an independent part of CP Ships. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
